blocks.html: From Paul to the church in Corinth:

items.html: Blessed be God, even the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies, and the God of all comfort;
Who comforteth us in all our tribulation, that we may be able to comfort them which are in any trouble, by the comfort wherewith we ourselves are comforted of God.
For as the sufferings of Christ abound in us, so our consolation also aboundeth by Christ.

And whether we be afflicted, it is for your consolation and salvation, which is effectual in the enduring of the same sufferings which we also suffer: or whether we be comforted, it is for your consolation and salvation.
And our hope of you is stedfast, knowing, that as ye are partakers of the sufferings, so shall ye be also of the consolation.
For we would not, brethren, have you ignorant of our trouble which came to us in Asia, that we were pressed out of measure, above strength, insomuch that we despaired even of life:
But we had the sentence of death in ourselves, that we should not trust in ourselves, but in God which raiseth the dead:
Who delivered us from so great a death, and doth deliver: in whom we trust that he will yet deliver us;
Ye also helping together by prayer for us, that for the gift bestowed upon us by the means of many persons thanks may be given by many on our behalf.

For our rejoicing is this, the testimony of our conscience, that in simplicity and godly sincerity, not with fleshly wisdom, but by the grace of God, we have had our conversation in the world, and more abundantly to you-ward.
For we write none other things unto you, than what ye read or acknowledge; and I trust ye shall acknowledge even to the end;

blocks.html: Blessed be God, the father of mercies. [1]

items.html: As also ye have acknowledged us in part, that we are your rejoicing, even as ye also are ours in the day of the Lord Jesus.
And in this confidence I was minded to come unto you before, that ye might have a second benefit;
And to pass by you into Macedonia, and to come again out of Macedonia unto you, and of you to be brought on my way toward Judaea.
When I therefore was thus minded, did I use lightness? or the things that I purpose, do I purpose according to the flesh, that with me there should be yea yea, and nay nay?
But as God is true, our word toward you was not yea and nay.
For the Son of God, Jesus Christ, who was preached among you by us, even by me and Silvanus and Timothy, was not yea and nay, but in him was yea.
For all the promises of God in him are yea, and in him Amen, unto the glory of God by us.
Now he which stablisheth us with you in Christ, and hath anointed us, is God;
Who hath also sealed us, and given the earnest of the Spirit in our hearts.
Moreover I call God for a record upon my soul, that to spare you I came not as yet unto Corinth.
Not for that we have dominion over your faith, but are helpers of your joy: for by faith ye stand.

items.html: But I determined this with myself, that I would not come again to you in heaviness.

For out of much affliction and anguish of heart I wrote unto you with many tears; not that ye should be grieved, but that ye might know the love which I have more abundantly unto you.
But if any have caused grief, he hath not grieved me, but in part: that I may not overcharge you all.
Sufficient to such a man is this punishment, which was inflicted of many.
So that contrariwise ye ought rather to forgive him, and comfort him, lest perhaps such a one should be swallowed up with overmuch sorrow.
Wherefore I beseech you that ye would confirm your love toward him.
For to this end also did I write, that I might know the proof of you, whether ye be obedient in all things.

Lest Satan should get an advantage of us: for we are not ignorant of his devices.
Furthermore, when I came to Troas to preach Christ's gospel, and a door was opened unto me of the Lord,
I had no rest in my spirit, because I found not Titus my brother: but taking my leave of them, I went from thence into Macedonia.

For we are unto God a sweet savour of Christ, in them that are saved, and in them that perish:
to the one we are the savour of death unto death; and to the other the savour of life unto life. And who is sufficient for these things?

items.html: Would to God ye could bear with me a little in my folly: and indeed bear with me.

blocks.html:

I've chosen you as a virgin bride of Christ.

blocks.html: I worry that the serpent will trick you, as he did Eve. [1]

items.html: For if he that cometh preacheth another Jesus, whom we have not preached, or if ye receive another spirit, which ye have not received, or another gospel, which ye have not accepted, ye might well bear with him.

When someone preaches another Jesus, Spirit, or gospel

than the one I preached to you, you accept their preaching.

items.html: For I suppose I was not a whit behind the very chiefest apostles.

blocks.html: I may not speak as well, but my knowledge is greater.

items.html: Have I committed an offence in abasing myself that ye might be exalted, because I have preached to you the gospel of God freely?

blocks.html: I didn't charge you for my preaching.

items.html: I robbed other churches, taking wages of them, to do you service.

blocks.html:
I robbed other churches, [3]

taking wages that they paid me, to serve you.

items.html: As the truth of Christ is in me, no man shall stop me of this boasting in the regions of Achaia.
Wherefore? because I love you not? God knoweth.
But what I do, that I will do, that I may cut off occasion from them which desire occasion; that wherein they glory, they may be found even as we.

blocks.html: No one will stop me from this boasting.

items.html: For such are false apostles, deceitful workers, transforming themselves into the apostles of Christ.

blocks.html:
They are deceitful workers,

pretending to be the apostles of Christ.

items.html: And no marvel; for Satan himself is transformed into an angel of light.

blocks.html:
And it's no wonder.

Satan himself transforms himself into an angel of light.

items.html: Therefore it is no great thing if his ministers also be transformed as the ministers of righteousness; whose end shall be according to their works.

blocks.html: Their end will be according to their works. [4]
I'm just boasting here (I'm not speaking for God)

items.html: I say again, Let no man think me a fool; if otherwise, yet as a fool receive me, that I may boast myself a little.

blocks.html:
Don't think I'm a fool.

But if you do, let me boast a little.

items.html: That which I speak, I speak it not after the Lord, but as it were foolishly, in this confidence of boasting.

blocks.html:
I'm not saying any of this for the Lord,

I'm just foolishly boasting.

items.html: Seeing that many glory after the flesh, I will glory also.

blocks.html: Many glory after the flesh, so I'll glory too.

items.html: For ye suffer fools gladly, seeing ye yourselves are wise.

blocks.html: You are wise, so you suffer fools gladly.

items.html: For ye suffer, if a man bring you into bondage, if a man devour you, if a man take of you, if a man exalt himself, if a man smite you on the face.

blocks.html: You let them enslave you, devour you, steal from you, and hit you on the face.

items.html: I speak as concerning reproach, as though we had been weak. Howbeit whereinsoever any is bold, (I speak foolishly,) I am bold also.

blocks.html: Well, I'm a bold as they are.

items.html: Are they Hebrews? so am I. Are they Israelites? so am I. Are they the seed of Abraham? so am I.

blocks.html: Are they Hebrews, Israelites, the seed of Abraham, well so am I?

items.html: Are they ministers of Christ? (I speak as a fool) I am more; in labours more abundant, in stripes above measure, in prisons more frequent, in deaths oft.

blocks.html:
Are they ministers of Christ? (I speak as a fool.) I am more.

I've worked harder, been beaten and imprisoned more frequently, and I've often been in danger of death.

items.html: Of the Jews five times received I forty stripes save one.

blocks.html: The Jews gave me 39 lashes five times.

items.html: Thrice was I beaten with rods, once was I stoned, thrice I suffered shipwreck, a night and a day I have been in the deep;

blocks.html: I've been beaten with rods, stoned, shipwrecked three times, and spend a night and a day in the depths of the sea.

items.html: In journeyings often, in perils of waters, in perils of robbers, in perils by mine own countrymen, in perils by the heathen, in perils in the city, in perils in the wilderness, in perils in the sea, in perils among false brethren;

blocks.html: I've been endangered by robbers, countrymen, and heathens. In the city, wilderness, and at sea.

items.html: In weariness and painfulness, in watchings often, in hunger and thirst, in fastings often, in cold and nakedness.

blocks.html: I've suffered pain, hunger, thirst, fasting, cold, and nakedness.

items.html: Beside those things that are without, that which cometh upon me daily, the care of all the churches.

blocks.html: And I through it all I took care of the churches.

items.html: Who is weak, and I am not weak? who is offended, and I burn not?
If I must needs glory, I will glory of the things which concern mine infirmities.
The God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, which is blessed for evermore, knoweth that I lie not.

blocks.html: God has blessed me, knowing that I don't lie.

items.html: In Damascus the governor under Aretas the king kept the city of the Damascenes with a garrison, desirous to apprehend me:
And through a window in a basket was I let down by the wall, and escaped his hands.

blocks.html: I even escaped through a window once in a basket while being lowered down a wall.

footnotes.html:
As the serpent beguiled Eve through his subtilty (v.3)

Paul believed the silly talking snake story in Genesis 3.

Young Earth Creationists use this verse to show that Paul believed the creation story in Gen.3:1-6. So it must be true.

The Gospel -- Evidence for Creation

I suppose I was not a whit behind the very chiefest apostles. (v.5)

Paul sarcastically refers to his rivals here as "the very cheifest apostles", or as the New Revised Standard Version puts it, "super-apostles".

I robbed other churches. (v.8)

Paul set an example for televangelists by robbing (taking wages from) churches, and using the money for other things.

Whose end shall be according to their works. (v.15)

Is salvation by faith alone?

who was caught up in paradise and heard unspeakable words,

words which are against the law to utter.

I'll give guys like that the glory.

the messenger of Satan, to constrain me.

blocks.html:
He said,

My grace is enough for you.

My strength is perfect in weakness.
I'm as good as those super apostles

blocks.html:
I'm a fool for glorifying myself, but you made me do it.

You should have praised me,

since I'm at least as good as those super apostles.

I'm ready to come visit you a third time.

I promise not to be a burden to you.

blocks.html:
I'll gladly spend for you.

Anyway, I didn't burden you.

As the scripture says, "Two or three witnesses are required to establish the truth of a statement." [1]

items.html: I told you before, and foretell you, as if I were present, the second time; and being absent now I write to them which heretofore have sinned, and to all other, that, if I come again, I will not spare:

blocks.html:
I told you before and I'm telling you again,

I'll punish those of you who have sinned.

items.html: Since ye seek a proof of Christ speaking in me, which to you-ward is not weak, but is mighty in you.
For though he was crucified through weakness, yet he liveth by the power of God. For we also are weak in him, but we shall live with him by the power of God toward you.

blocks.html:
You'll have proof that Christ speaks in me

when he deals with you.

items.html: Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves. Know ye not your own selves, how that Jesus Christ is in you, except ye be reprobates?
But I trust that ye shall know that we are not reprobates.
Now I pray to God that ye do no evil; not that we should appear approved, but that ye should do that which is honest, though we be as reprobates.
For we can do nothing against the truth, but for the truth.
For we are glad, when we are weak, and ye are strong: and this also we wish, even your perfection.
Therefore I write these things being absent, lest being present I should use sharpness, according to the power which the Lord hath given me to edification, and not to destruction.

blocks.html:
Test yourself to see if you are a reprobate.

If you know for sure that Jesus Christ is in you,

you're not a reprobate.

Otherwise, you are.
